agree.reason: The checkpoints, the fallback options and the respectful staffing paragraph give the two advertising-background members reasons to vote yes, but the memo invents a $17,000 shortfall and leaves its funding as a bracketed placeholder, which gives the skeptics an easy reason to hold off.

honest.reason: The memo says the $47,000 drop took two years when it happened in one, and it states as fact that the decline is industry-wide and that more selling won't reverse it, though nothing in the brief supports either claim.

works_the_facts.reason: The pilot figures are worked correctly ($20,000 a year, 1.5% of the list, 875 members as 6% of the list), but the ad trend uses the wrong pace, which weakens the projection and hides the strongest true number.

right_comparison.reason: Ads fell 36% in one year, so if nothing changes they would bring in about $54,000 in 2026 and about $34,000 in 2027, not $67,000; against that trend, $50,000 from membership would beat ads in year one instead of leaving a gap.

qualification.reason: The quarterly member targets have dates and numbers, and a miss of more than 20% at June leads to named options, so the board can check progress, though 'bring the board options' is a fairly soft consequence.

objections.reason: The memo deals with the ad sales lead and offers a fallback that includes non-display advertising, but it raises a year-one revenue-gap worry that the correct ad trend would have answered.

fit.reason: It is a one-page memo with clear headings and a decision request at the top, but the bracketed placeholders leave key choices unmade.
